newsitem.title: USA: Storage Dimensions reports Q2 loss.
newsitem.headline: Storage Dimensions reports Q2 loss.

text.p: Storage Dimensions Inc Monday reported a second quarter loss of $1.2 million or $0.16 a share, versus a profit of $271,000, or $0.05 a share, for the same period a year ago.
Net sales for the second quarter were $16.6 million, or 9 percent below net sales of $18.3 million reported in the same period a year ago.

The company attributed the results to four primary factors -- softness in the PC-LAN market, price erosion on disk drive components, below-plan staffing of the company's end-user sales force and expenses related to the RAIDPro product introduction.
The company the shortfall was further amplified in late June by a product return taken from a single customer which resulted in a one-time reduction in net sales of $1.3 million.
The customer, whose business was severely impacted by recent price erosion of disk drives, was no longer able to satisfy payment terms with Storage Dimensions, the company said.

"Although this sale was not made on a contingent basis and the customer had no legal right to return such equipment, Storage Dimensions' management initiated this return in order to avoid the possibility of larger costs," the company said. "The company expects to complete reselling the returned equipment, consisting of unused, standard products, during the third quarter.

Net sales for the first six months of 1997 rose to $37.5 million, 9 percent above net sales of $34.3 million reported in the same period a year ago. Net loss for the first six months was $480,000, or $0.07 per share, versus net income of $390,000, or $0.07 per share, for the same period a year ago.
